- Workflow issues: [workflow_templates/issues](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/workflow_templates/issues)

nodes.title: READ ME!
widgets_values:
## Settings

Enter the desired iterations (clips), resolution, steps for the video (20 is the usual optimum), steps for the injected last frames (usually want more for better quality), and clip length. Shorter clips will generate a lot faster but will repeat the anchor frames more often.

Enter desired project folder where generated latents and video files will be saved (output/longrun by default).

IMPORTANT: 
- Always remove all files from the project folder to avoid mixed up latent/video links and to reset workflow loop logic. The number of files is being used as loop index.
- If you keep old latents in the project folder latent subfolder, the workflow will continue generating from the last latent and then finally join the videos, when the input audio is exhausted. Thus it is possible to easily recover from an interrupted generation.
- Do not switch workflow tabs while generating.

The workflow uses a hacky custom node for workflow retriggering. Another option was to use ComfyUI native Start Loop / End Loop, but it is slow to start because of heavy cache calculations. For example, if the audio is split into 100 segments, Start Loop may take 5 minutes to prepare the cache.

Use reference images as usual and adjust the prompt to your needs.
If Fantastic H3 Media Loader UI collapses, switch to another workflow and then back. It's a known ComfyUI bug waiting for a fix, see [#15331](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI_frontend/pull/15331).


## Anchor frames

To keep quality consistent, the workflow injects a single end-frame into conditioning. By default, the frame is generated using the same prompt. However, in some cases it might cause the prompt beginning actions to be rendered. To fix this, one second (22 frames for Minimax latent grid) of video can be generated, and usually the model tries to squeeze the entire prompt execution and ends with the last action in the prompt. The workflow will extract and use the last 1-frame from the 1+4 pattern at the 22 frames tail, thus it will be very likely the last action of the prompt, as expected. Alternatively, you can use any other way to generate last frames - other models, separate prompts and references etc. Just wire your solution to the Set_endframes_latent node.

TODO: implementing simple nodes to pass in a list of shot prompts and last-frame prompts that will be used as the iteration source.


## Outputs

The final video is saved in project folder, video subfolder. To avoid audio VAE recoding artifacts, the original audio is added to the final video. To save every clip (will be slower), enable the "Decode clip video" group. All the generated latents are saved in the project's latents subfolder for later editing and rejoining, if needed. You can assemble them also separately using concat_latents_and_decode.json workflow. Remove them when generating a new project.

## Regenerating a clip

If you want to regenerate one of the clips and preserve smooth transitions from the previous and next clips, find the corresponding latent by time. You can find the latent from the file name of the latent you want to regenerate (e.g. clip_n_00003_t_12s_00001.avlatent contains the video after 12 seconds). Use retake_longtalk_latent_part.json workflow to regenerate it. After generating the new latent and reviewing it, delete the old latent and rename the new latent to match the old latent's name. Then use concat_latents_and_decode.json workflow to assemble the final video (or use your video editor with the regenerated clip).

nodes.title: Calc overlap latent grid frames, snap down
Last frame latent
widgets_values:
For simple scenes with continuous repetitive actions (talking, dancing, fighting) a single frame often may be enough.

For more dynamic scenes use at least 22 frame latent to let the model squeeze the entire prompt into the frames and then in "Last frame conditioning" group take the latent token that has 1 frame, according to MiniMax frame distribution 17k+5 (1444414) formula.
Or you can obtain end frames any other way (generate with another prompt, load pregenerated images based on filename index for each clip, generate with another model using the same references etc.)
